provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The program finds every 4-connected component of the background colour (palette[0]). It accepts a component as a frame interior when all three tests pass. (1) The component exactly fills its bounding box. (2) Every in-grid cell of the 8-neighbour ring around that box is wire colour (palette[5]); ring cells that fall off the grid are allowed. (3) For each of the four ring corners, the cell one step further along each of the two frame edges is not wire. Test 3 is what separates a real frame corner from the crossing of two straight wires. Accepted interiors are painted palette[4]; every other cell is copied unchanged. The test set (rectangle, full ring, corner extensions in both edge directions) maps onto itself under every rotation and reflection. Because of that, the same direct visible-coordinate mechanism is correct for all eight d4 values, and nothing is rotated or un-rotated. Colour roles are fixed palette constants rather than guessed from pixel frequency, so ties in colour counts cannot change the result. This is the archived solver's mechanism rewritten with palette-specialised colours. By hand I traced it against the rule's described results for the three training pairs and the test (including the 1-cell interior at (2,0), the border-cut 3-cell interior and the 1x2 interior at the left edge). It agrees with all of them. No code was actually run; the host's fixture and fresh-pair checks are the real verification.
draft_notes.limitations: Because the rule is D4-symmetric, d4 has no effect on the emitted code. The program relies on the generator's domain (exactly one wire colour, background palette[0]) and ignores the demonstrations. One possible constructor-domain caveat needs host review. A background region bounded only by the grid edge and a straight wire would also pass all three tests and be filled. For that to happen the region would need to be a rectangle ringed by wire and the edge, with no corner extensions. By my reading of the generator it seems hard to reach: boxes are at most 7 wide in grids at least 10 wide, and lines start at box walls. The archived solver shares this behaviour. I found no fixture contradicting the uniform rule, and I noticed no generator indexing bug or hidden random tie-break that the solver depends on.

independent_source_review.mechanism: The program takes each 4-connected component of the background colour (palette[0]) and fills it with palette[4] when three tests pass. (1) The component exactly fills its bounding box. (2) Every in-grid cell of the 8-neighbour ring around that box is wire colour (palette[5]). (3) At each of the four ring corners, the cell one step further outward along each frame edge is not wire. This is the archived transform with palette-specialised colour constants. It runs directly in visible coordinates with no untransform or retransform wrapper. That is sound because tests 1-3 map onto themselves under all eight D4 operations.
evidence: The constructor draws each box as a full grey rectangle and then sets the interior (row+1..row+tall-2, col+1..col+wide-2) to black in the input and yellow in the output. Lines are drawn grey in both grids. So the label is exactly 'box interiors become yellow', with no hidden latent beyond geometry that is visible in the input.

Boxes never touch. The box overlap test uses a strict '<', so any two boxes are separated by at least one cell in rows or columns. All randomness affects placement only, never which cells are labelled.

Lines never cross a box interior or run alongside a box wall. Every line path is checked against the bitmap at offsets -1, 0 and +1 across its width. Pair lines use lorow=max+1 and hirow=min-2, and edge lines use randint(col+1, col+wide-2). This puts every line on an interior row or column of the box it attaches to, so a line meets a wall as a T-junction, never at the wall's corner.

Every in-grid corner of a real box interior passes test 3. The outward cell (A.row-1, A.col) or (A.row, A.col-1) could only be wire through one of three cases, and each is impossible. A neighbouring box would need to be adjacent with no gap, which the overlap test forbids. A line through that cell would have a box cell within its -1/0/+1 check, so it would have been rejected. A line ending there would require its target box to overlap A.

False positives are rejected by test 3. A region bounded by lines has a corner at a crossing (plus shape), at a line endpoint beside a wall (T shape: wall continues, or line continues), or at the grid edge. Lines never run edge to edge. Lines at row 0, row height-1, column 0 or column width-1 cannot form a ring side, because of the r ≥ row+1 condition, the row > 0 and row+1 < height guard, and c ≤ width-3. So every in-grid corner of a gap region has wire continuing beyond it.
Boxes cut by the border have their off-grid ring cells and corners ignored, which matches the col ∈ [-1, width-wide+1] range. That includes 1-wide interiors from wide=3.

The fixtures fit the uniform rule. Examples are the 1-cell interior at (2,0) in train pair 2, the border-cut 3-cell interiors, and the test's 1x2 interior at the left edge. The host audit passed 16 fixture variants, 1000 fresh pairs and 8000 augmented checks.

Colour roles come from the palette rather than from frequency, so there are no count ties. The fill colour palette[4] appears in every demonstration output. e73095fd is not in the colour-evidence task list, and the program needs no arbitrary lookup association.
nonblocking_limits: The program ignores the demonstrations. It assumes the generator's domain: exactly one wire colour palette[5] on background palette[0].

The program would also fill a hypothetical rectangle bounded only by straight wire and the grid edge, with no true in-grid L-corners. By source tracing this is unreachable, because no line spans edge to edge or runs along rows 0 or height-1 or columns 0 or width-1. The archived solver behaves the same way.
d4 has no effect on the emitted code. This is justified because the detection predicate is D4-invariant; it is not a wrapper.
Accept means the source review found no blocking issue. It does not prove correctness outside the constructor's domain.
required_context_checks: Confirm that the host's augmented checks remapped background, wire and fill through the same palette passed to build_program (palette[0], palette[5], palette[4]).
No colour-evidence check applies to e73095fd. The standard D4 conflicting-answer rejection is sufficient.

host_review.resolution: Reviewed constructor invariants, visible-coordinate solver, fixture agreement and documented out-of-domain branches. Source hashes match passing audit.
host_review.augmentation_evidence: All eight D4 transforms are checked in audit; d4=7 is its final loop index. Palette is bijective and shared across all episode pairs.
host_review.limitations: Finite execution/domain evidence, not proof of unrestricted generalization or complete identifiability.
